chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: 'Whoever acknowledges upon himself, in the presence of the Imam, the right of one of the Muslims, it is not incumbent upon the Imam to establish the Hadd (penalty) upon him, which he acknowledged in his presence, until the owner of the Hadd right or his guardian is present, so that he may claim his right.'

key_terms.إِقْرَار: Confession or acknowledgment of a right or crime
key_terms.إِمَام: The Imam or judge exercising authority
key_terms.حَدّ: Hadd, a fixed Islamic penalty for specific crimes
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْحَقّ: The owner of the right (the victim)

ai.seo_question: When does the Imam wait for the victim before enforcing a Hadd penalty after a confession?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith distinguishes between *Hudud* (fixed penalties for God's sake) and *Huquq al-Nas* (rights of people), establishing that the Imam's authority to enforce the public penalty is suspended until the private right is settled. This reflects the principle that the victim holds the primary claim, and their absence or waiver can prevent the execution of the *Hadd*, highlighting the interplay between divine justice and individual entitlement in the legal system.
